imp.voice_memo: Poe writes as a haunted witness, not a reporter. The voice is almost always first-person, confessional, and over-rational—a narrator who marshals exact measurements and learned authorities to prove his sanity while the prose itself shows him coming apart. His signature instrument is the long periodic sentence: clause stacked upon clause, qualification upon qualification, the breath held and held until a dash ruptures it and re-aims the thought. Read him aloud and you feel the dashes everywhere, suspending, interrupting, escalating—"and the six hours of deadly terror which I then endured have broken me up body and soul." Against these long swells he sets sudden short declaratives that land like blows: "Here died my mother. Herein was I born." Repetition is his incantation—he echoes a word until it loses or gains meaning ("down, down, down"; "now—now"; "Danced! Danced!"), and italicizes the single term that carries the horror. His diction is antique and Latinate, sonorous and a little overripe: tenebrous, ineffable, sepulchral, immethodical. He moves characteristically from abstraction toward dread, opening on a metaphysical generalization and descending, particular by particular, into the concrete. Crucially, he grounds the supernatural in clinical precision—latitudes, fathoms, the exact angle of a funnel, the minute on a watch—so the impossible feels measured and inevitable. The senses pile toward suffocation; the body is always in extremity, hair whitening in a day, eyes starting from their sockets. He addresses the reader directly, anticipating disbelief. And beneath the gravity runs a streak of grotesque, deadpan comedy. To ghostwrite Poe: testify, don't summarize; let the sentence strain and snap; make terror exact.
